Teleport is NOT a password vault. Its model eliminates static credentials entirely via short-lived X.509 certificates; no credential vaulting, check-out/check-in, or automated rotation of stored passwords. See: goteleport.com/blog/zero-standing-privileges-vs-credential-vaulting/ — 'Teleport was built around identity and verification, not vaults.' Customers needing classical password vaulting must use a separate tool (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, CyberArk).

evidence_quote: Every privileged session proxied through Teleport with full identity context
notes: Certificate-based proxy for SSH, RDP/Windows Desktop, Kubernetes, Database, and App access. No direct firewall holes required; all traffic funnelled through Teleport Proxy Service. Strong isolation — market-leading for cloud-native environments.

evidence_quote: Captures entire PTY output; supports BPF-level enhanced recording
notes: Full session recording (node-sync, node, proxy-sync, proxy modes) for SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, database, and app sessions. Enhanced BPF recording captures syscalls. 1-year default retention; SIEM-exportable structured audit logs.

evidence_quote: Fine-grained ephemeral privileges eliminate all static standing access
notes: Teleport Access Requests via CLI, Web UI, Slack, PagerDuty, Jira, ServiceNow. Automatic expiry enforced by cert TTL. Access Graph surfaces standing-privilege count. Dual-authorisation and session-moderator options. Market-leading JIT for infrastructure.

This is outside Teleport's architectural scope. EPM requires a dedicated tool (e.g., BeyondTrust EPM, CyberArk EPM).
